:::{#thm-moore-penrose-full-rank}
#### The Moore-Penrose inverse of a matrix of full column rank or full row rank

Let $\matr{A}$ be an $m \times n$ [matrix](linear-algebra-matrices.qmd#def-matrix).

1. If $\matr{A}$ has full column rank (@def-full-column-rank), then
   $\tp{\matr{A}} \matr{A}$ is [invertible](linear-algebra-special-matrices.qmd#def-matrix-inverse) and
   $\matr{A}^+ = \inv{(\tp{\matr{A}} \matr{A})}\,\tp{\matr{A}}$.
2. If $\operatorname{rank}(\matr{A}) = m$, then
   $\matr{A} \tp{\matr{A}}$ is invertible and
   $\matr{A}^+ = \tp{\matr{A}}\,\inv{(\matr{A} \tp{\matr{A}})}$.

:::

::: proof

By @thm-moore-penrose-unique, it is enough to show that the [matrix](linear-algebra-matrices.qmd#def-matrix) $\matr{G}$ named in each part
satisfies the four conditions of @def-moore-penrose.

**Part 1.**
$\tp{\matr{A}} \matr{A}$ is [invertible](linear-algebra-special-matrices.qmd#def-matrix-inverse) by @thm-gram-invertible.
Let $\matr{G} = \inv{(\tp{\matr{A}} \matr{A})}\,\tp{\matr{A}}$.
Then

$$
\ba
\matr{G} \matr{A}
&= \inv{(\tp{\matr{A}} \matr{A})}\,\tp{\matr{A}} \matr{A}
&& \text{(definition of } \matr{G} \text{)}
\\
&= \matr{I}_n.
&& \text{(@def-matrix-inverse)}
\ea
$$

- Condition 4: $\tp{(\matr{G} \matr{A})} = \tp{\matr{I}_n} = \matr{I}_n = \matr{G} \matr{A}$.
- Condition 1: $\matr{A} \matr{G} \matr{A} = \matr{A} \matr{I}_n = \matr{A}$.
- Condition 2: $\matr{G} \matr{A} \matr{G} = \matr{I}_n \matr{G} = \matr{G}$.
- Condition 3:
  $\tp{(\matr{A} \matr{G})}
  = \matr{A}\,\tp{\paren{\inv{(\tp{\matr{A}} \matr{A})}}}\,\tp{\matr{A}}
  = \matr{A}\,\inv{\tp{(\tp{\matr{A}} \matr{A})}}\,\tp{\matr{A}}
  = \matr{A}\,\inv{(\tp{\matr{A}} \matr{A})}\,\tp{\matr{A}}
  = \matr{A} \matr{G}$,
  by @thm-transpose-product, @thm-inverse-transpose, and because $\tp{\matr{A}} \matr{A}$ is [symmetric](linear-algebra-special-matrices.qmd#def-symmetric-matrix).

**Part 2.**
$\operatorname{rank}(\matr{A} \tp{\matr{A}}) = \operatorname{rank}(\matr{A}) = m$ (@thm-rank-transpose),
and $\matr{A} \tp{\matr{A}}$ is $m \times m$,
so it is invertible (@thm-invertible-rank).
Let $\matr{G} = \tp{\matr{A}}\,\inv{(\matr{A} \tp{\matr{A}})}$.
Then $\matr{A} \matr{G} = \matr{A} \tp{\matr{A}}\,\inv{(\matr{A} \tp{\matr{A}})} = \matr{I}_m$ (@def-matrix-inverse).

- Condition 3: $\tp{(\matr{A} \matr{G})} = \tp{\matr{I}_m} = \matr{I}_m = \matr{A} \matr{G}$.
- Condition 1: $\matr{A} \matr{G} \matr{A} = \matr{I}_m \matr{A} = \matr{A}$.
- Condition 2: $\matr{G} \matr{A} \matr{G} = \matr{G} \matr{I}_m = \matr{G}$.
- Condition 4:
  $\tp{(\matr{G} \matr{A})}
  = \tp{\matr{A}}\,\tp{\paren{\inv{(\matr{A} \tp{\matr{A}})}}}\,\matr{A}
  = \tp{\matr{A}}\,\inv{(\matr{A} \tp{\matr{A}})}\,\matr{A}
  = \matr{G} \matr{A}$,
  by @thm-transpose-product, @thm-inverse-transpose, and because $\matr{A} \tp{\matr{A}}$ is symmetric.

:::

{{< slidebreak >}}

:::{#exm-moore-penrose-full-rank}
#### Moore-Penrose inverses of a column and a row

The $2 \times 1$ [matrix](linear-algebra-matrices.qmd#def-matrix) $\matr{A} = \begin{bmatrix} 1 \\ 1 \end{bmatrix}$ has [full column rank](linear-algebra-subspaces.qmd#def-full-column-rank),
and $\tp{\matr{A}} \matr{A} = \begin{bmatrix} 2 \end{bmatrix}$, so

$$
\begin{aligned}
\matr{A}^+ &= \tfrac{1}{2} \begin{bmatrix} 1 & 1 \end{bmatrix} \\
&= \begin{bmatrix} \tfrac{1}{2} & \tfrac{1}{2} \end{bmatrix}.
\end{aligned}
$$

Then $\matr{A}^+ \matr{A} = \begin{bmatrix} 1 \end{bmatrix}$,
and $\matr{A} \matr{A}^+ = \begin{bmatrix} \tfrac{1}{2} & \tfrac{1}{2} \\ \tfrac{1}{2} & \tfrac{1}{2} \end{bmatrix}$ is [symmetric](linear-algebra-special-matrices.qmd#def-symmetric-matrix).

The $1 \times 2$ matrix $\matr{B} = \begin{bmatrix} 1 & 1 \end{bmatrix}$ has [rank](linear-algebra-subspaces.qmd#def-rank) $1$, which is its count of rows,
and $\matr{B} \tp{\matr{B}} = \begin{bmatrix} 2 \end{bmatrix}$, so

$$
\begin{aligned}
\matr{B}^+ &= \begin{bmatrix} 1 \\ 1 \end{bmatrix} \tfrac{1}{2} \\
&= \begin{bmatrix} \tfrac{1}{2} \\ \tfrac{1}{2} \end{bmatrix}.
\end{aligned}
$$

:::
